claims.text: High configurational entropy drives spatially uniform segregation of oxide-forming elements at the alloy surface.
Uniform surface segregation of oxide-forming elements facilitates rapid formation of a continuous protective oxide layer.
Uniform surface segregation of oxide-forming elements facilitates retention of an adherent protective oxide layer during high-temperature oxidation.
The relevant initial state is a single-phase, compositionally homogeneous high-entropy alloy containing oxide-forming elements such as Cr and Al.
A homogeneous elemental distribution permits spatially uniform surface segregation of oxide-forming elements.
High configurational entropy reduces local compositional fluctuations.
Reduced local compositional fluctuations promote early and spatially even surface segregation of reactive elements such as Cr and Al.
Surface-enriched Cr and Al form a continuous and adherent protective oxide scale.
A continuous and adherent protective oxide scale slows further oxidation.
Under matched oxidation conditions, the HEA will form a more uniform oxide layer than a similar conventional lower-entropy alloy.
Under matched oxidation conditions, the HEA oxide layer will be more adherent than that of a similar conventional lower-entropy alloy.
Under matched oxidation conditions, the HEA oxide layer will grow more slowly than that of a similar conventional lower-entropy alloy.
The more uniform, adherent, and slowly growing oxide layer will provide the HEA with enhanced oxidation resistance.
Conventional lower-configurational-entropy alloys with similar nominal compositions typically form less uniform oxide scales.
Conventional lower-configurational-entropy alloys with similar nominal compositions typically form more porous or spall-prone oxide scales.
The proposed behavior requires adequate concentrations of oxide-forming elements.
High moisture or extreme oxygen partial pressures may alter the proposed oxidation behavior.
